Elections

November 3, 2026 General Election

Voter Eligibility:

Only voters who are United States Citizens are eligible to vote in the General Election.

Early Voting:

  • All active registered voters in Burlington will be mailed a ballot by October 1st. To check your voter registration status, visit https://vote.vermont.gov 
  • If you do not receive your ballot by October 8th, and would like to vote early, please contact the Clerk Treasurer’s Office by phone or email, or visit the office during business hours no later than Monday, November 2nd at 1:00pm. 
  • Carefully follow all of the instructions when completing your absentee ballot. Be sure to SIGN the envelope and SEAL your ballot inside of it or your vote will not count.
  • Return the voted ballot: 
    1. At City Hall:
      • Monday through Friday, 8am – 1pm; 1:30pm - 4:30pm until October 30th.
      • On Monday, November 2nd, from 8am – 1pm.
    2. At a Ballot Drop Box located at:
      • City Hall – Main Street side of the building across from the Flynn Theater
      • Department of Public Works – 645 Pine Street
      • Fire Station #2 – 132 North Avenue, rear of building 
      • Robert Miller Community Center – 130 Gosse Court
      • Fire Station #3 – 20 Mansfield Avenue
    3. By Mail:
      • If returning your ballot by mail, we recommend that you mail your ballot back no later than October 20th.  
    4. At your polling place on Election Day between 7:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m. A list of polling places can be found at https://www.burlingtonvt.gov/CT/Maps-Wards-State-Districts-and-Polling-Places

Election Day Voting:

  • Polling places will be open from 7:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m. on Election Day
    • Bring the ballot that was sent to you in the mail with you. If you did not receive a ballot or do not bring it with you, you will still be able to vote. However, you will be asked to sign an affidavit first.
    • Voters who are unable to get to their polling place, due to illness or disability, may contact the Clerk's office to request curbside voting at their polling place, electronic ballot delivery, or home ballot delivery by Justices of the Peace.

Important Dates:

  • October 1st – Ballots Mailed to all registered voters
  • November 2nd, 1pm – deadline to register to vote online or in the Clerk/ Treasurers Office before Election Day; Election Day registration is available at your polling place on November 3rd. 
  • November 2nd, 4:30 p.m. – deadline to drop off your voted ballot in a drop box
  • November 3rd – Election Day! Polls open 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m.

Language Access

  • العربية (Arabic) , မြန်မာစာ (Burmese), Français (French), नेपाली (Nepali), Soomaali (Somali), and Kiswahili (Swahili) translations of election information are available at https://www.burlingtonvt.gov/165/Election-Language-Support
  • If you need an interpreter on Election Day, or for early voting, please ask a staff member at the Clerk’s office or an election official. You have the right to a FREE interpreter. The City provides interpreter services for over 300 languages.
  1. Confirm Your Voter Registration

United State's Citizens can search Burlington's Voter Checklist at the Vermont Secretary of State's website to Verify their Registration and Ward. Legal Residents who are not United States Citizens can confirm their Registration by calling the Clerk Treasurer's Office at 802-865-7000.

Burlington residents can vote in three types of elections:

  • Burlington Elections (local items only, municipal and school - open to all legal residents, regardless of citizenship status)
  • State Elections (only open to United States citizens)
  • Federal Elections (only open to United States citizens)
  1. Register to Vote
  • In Person: Voters can register at the Clerk Treasurer's Office until the Friday before an election. Voters can also register to vote at their polling place on Election Day.
  • Online:United States Citizens may register online
  • By mail: Complete and return one of the following forms to 149 Church Street, Burlington, VT 05401:
    • For United States Citizens: Vermont Voter Registration Form
    • For Burlington residents who are not United States Citizens: City of Burlington All Legal Resident Voter Registration Form (PDF). Translations of the City of Burlington All Legal Resident Registration Form are available in: Arabic | العربية (PDF) - Burmese | မြန်မာစာ (PDF) - French | Français (PDF) - Nepali | नेपाली (PDF) - Somali | Soomaali (PDF) - Swahili | Kiswahili (PDF)
